newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says to cut deposit rate to 2.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says to cut deposit rate to 2.6 pct.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Friday it will cut the interest rate it pays to other ministries for their long-term deposits by 0.1 percentage point to 2.6 percent, effective from May 9.
The rate of 2.6 percent would be a record low and follow a fall in the coupon rate of the latest auctioned 10-year Japanese government bonds (JGBs), on which the deposit rate is customarily set.
The coupon rate fell to a record low of 2.4 percent for the 10-year JGB to be issued on May 20 from 2.5 percent for the April issue.

The MOF's Trust Fund Bureau channels funds raised via deposits made by the Health Ministry and the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies for the fiscal investment and loan programme (FILP).
The programme is widely known as Japan's "second budget" for the role it plays in supplementing the state budget.
